editorial:
Imagine finding out your time is running out and deciding the best way to spend it is chasing a ghost from your past. That is exactly what happens to Se-yeon, who drops a bombshell on her husband, Jin-bong. She wants him to help her track down her first love before she passes away. It sounds like a recipe for a huge fight, but instead, it turns into a road trip that forces the couple to look at their own marriage. You get a mix of sadness and sweetness as they revisit old memories and rediscover why they fell in love in the first place. The vibe is very soft and emotional, making you think about your own relationships.

The acting is what really sells this story because the chemistry between the leads feels real and lived-in. While the pace is a bit slow in the middle, the music keeps you emotionally connected to the journey. If you enjoy stories that make you cry but leave you feeling warm inside, you will love this one. For the best experience, I suggest streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the pretty scenery, or you can rent it on Apple TV for a cozy movie night at home.
endingExplained: As the search continues, Se-yeon realizes that her first love was just a sweet memory, not something she actually needs in her final days. She discovers that the real love of her life has been Jin-bong all along. The movie ends with her passing away peacefully, surrounded by the love of her husband. It wraps up by showing that the journey was never about finding an ex, but about saying a beautiful goodbye to her partner.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heartfelt stories about love and loss.
